newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister's family to sue over Soviet report.
newsitem.headline: French minister's family to sue over Soviet report.

text.p: The family of late French defence minister Charles Hernu said on Monday it would sue a French magazine for saying that Hernu acted as an agent for the Soviet bloc in the 1950s and 1960s.

"I will file a legal action against L'Express because, having grown certain there is no truth to this dossier, the most natural path is the legal one," Patrice Hernu, one of the late minister's sons, told reporters.

Patrice Hernu, who met a senior aide to President Jacques Chirac in Paris on Monday, said his talks at the Elysee presidential palace reinforced his belief that the report in the current edition of the weekly news magazine L'Express was wrong.
L'Express said that Charles Hernu, who was defence minister from 1981-1985 and died in 1990, worked for the Bulgarian, Romanian and Soviet secret services for at least a decade from 1953.
Patrice Hernu said the family would sue "at least L'Express" for publishing unproved allegations against his father. He also urged France to lift official secrecy around the case.

Late French president Francois Mitterrand was briefed on the suspicions about Hernu in 1992 by Jacques Fournet, then head of France's DST counter-intelligence services, after Fournet received a dossier from east European spy services.

Fournet said after the L'Express report that the DST took the charges seriously enough to inform Mitterrand but was unable to verify them. Mitterrand ordered the reports to be kept secret, arguing Hernu could not defend himself.
